To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CMSIS-NN: 1. is the first open-source library of efficient neural network kernels for Arm Cortex-M processors, 2. achieves 4.9 times energy efficiency improvement for neural network inference on Cortex-M4 processors, 3. achieves 4X runtime improvement for neural network classification on Cortex-M4, and 4. achieves 4 times energy efficiency improvement on Cortex-M7 processors.
the CMSIS-NN library of kernels achieves 4-6X performance improvement and 4-6x energy efficiency improvement over existing NN libraries.
the kernels in CMSIS-NN achieve 4.6x improvement in runtime/ throughput and 4.6-5.1x improvement in energy efficiency compared to the existing NN kernels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient neural network kernels for IoT edge devices based on Arm Cortex-M CPUs.

the development and optimization of efficient kernels to enable neural networks to execute on the Cortex-M processors, which are used in a variety of IoT edge devices, such as smart meters, smart home appliances, and wearable devices.
the design, implementation, and optimization of efficient neural network inference kernels for the Arm Cortex-M processors.

the proposed CMSIS-NN library provides a set of efficient and portable NN kernels that can be easily used in NN applications for Arm Cortex-M processors.
